title: High-order correlations and ultrafast Wigner negativities in bright-squeezed-vacuum-driven high-harmonic generation
authors: Sebastián de-la-Peña, Heiko Appel, Marcelo F. Ciappina, Ofer Neufeld, Angel Rubio
abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a prototypical strong-field process in which intense light drives matter to emit radiation at integer multiples of the driving frequency. Extending HHG into the quantum-optical regime offers new opportunities to probe and control strongly nonlinear light-matter interactions using nonclassical states of light. Yet describing this regime requires a fully quantum treatment of the correlated electron-photon dynamics, which becomes computationally challenging for broadband, strongly squeezed fields. Here we solve the quantum-electrodynamical dynamics of a two-level system driven by bright squeezed vacuum in a converged multimode Hilbert space. Both the driving field and emitted harmonics are fully quantized, with the light-matter interaction treated nonperturbatively. This enables direct access to the multimode quantum state and its higher-order correlations beyond semiclassical sampling or perturbative descriptions. We show that squeezed-vacuum driving produces harmonic emission with qualitatively distinct second- and third-order photon correlations compared with coherent excitation. Moreover, back-action from the driven emitter strongly reshapes the incident squeezed field, generating pronounced Wigner-function negativities that evolve on attosecond timescales. Our results establish a fully quantum framework for broadband strong-field dynamics with squeezed light and provide a route to predicting and interpreting quantum-HHG experiments and their extension to more complex emitters.
summary: This theoretical study develops a fully quantum framework to model High-Harmonic Generation driven by bright-squeezed vacuum light. By solving the coupled quantum dynamics, the authors demonstrate that the nonclassical nature of the driving field leads to unique higher-order photon correlations and generates measurable, ultrafast Wigner-function negativities due to quantum back-action. This advances the understanding of nonlinear light-matter interactions in the quantum regime.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of fully quantum-mechanically describing High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) when driven by nonclassical, non-Gaussian light fields like bright-squeezed vacuum.
main_result: Squeezed-vacuum driving yields distinct higher-order photon correlations compared to coherent driving, and the back-action from the emitter generates measurable, time-evolving Wigner-function negativities on attosecond timescales.
method: The authors solve the full quantum-electrodynamical dynamics of a two-level system coupled to quantized light modes in a multimode Hilbert space, utilizing a squeezed-picture transformation for convergence.
model_or_system: The model uses a two-level system (TLS) as a benchmark for strong-field light-matter interaction, driven by a bright-squeezed vacuum (BSV) field, and quantizes both the driving and emitted harmonic fields.
key_observables: Second- and third-order photon correlations ($C^{(2)}, C^{(3)}$), Wigner function negativity volume ($V_{-}(t)$), and the full multimode quantum state.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($\xi$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega_R$), and the ratio of the energy gap to the driving frequency ($\Delta/\omega_L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the TLS approximation for the emitter and assumes that the continuum limit ($\Delta\omega 	o 0$) can be taken jointly with the infinite-photon limit ($|\xi| 	o \infty$) while keeping the physical driving strength finite.
figures_summary: Figures compare emission spectra for coherent vs. BSV driving, show second-order correlation spectra, and illustrate the time evolution of the Wigner distribution and the negativity volume $V_{-}(t)$ over attosecond timescales.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the fully quantum Hamiltonian, details the mathematical framework using the squeezed picture, calculates the correlation functions, and analyzes the time evolution of the quantum state's nonclassical features (Wigner negativity) due to back-action.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, fully quantum framework for strong-field light-matter interactions, moving beyond semiclassical approximations to predict and interpret quantum signatures like photon correlations and Wigner negativity in attosecond dynamics.
